known_bad_detection_method: Public wf_review_event dry run refused does_not council-readiness; two assertion inputs under one test name produced different SHA-256 identities and the older receipt accepted only the retry assertion.
limitations: Readiness examined plan feasibility and source provenance. Maintainer outcomes after release and teach-back efficacy await observation; product implementation and downstream trials have not run.
observed: Standard isolated red-team primer and independent architecture, security, QA, reality and rotating docs-contract seats recommend readiness unanimously. The renderer supports one thin pointer. The historical retry assertion matched its source digest in the chair's paired input, and the newer successful-response assertion did not. The public approval dry run rejected intent_fit=does_not. The strongest alternative is a blinded three-case AC-2 trial with the same test name: historical retry-only run, matched successful-response run, and unversioned green result. Each fixed seat favored it because answering unknown universally fails the matched cases. Replay AC-4 at the exact question with silence, decline and accept; verify configured nouns, separate teach-back consent, stable files, approvals and close eligibility.
proposition: Meeting AC-1 through AC-4 establishes the immediate source-linked handoff for the observed change, reader and wave.
safety_and_authorization: Local review evidence only; no external side effects.

known_bad_detection_method: Changed the disposable rendered Review offer to open the existing Review prompt itself. The destination identity assertion failed: review offer opens different existing prompt. It passed against the original route on all three hosts.

observed: AC-1 and AC-2: I followed Explain to the public lookups. Closed wave 23tcw returned 23tcu and 23tcv. The single 23tcu record confined its choice to cross-language builder and QA guidance, identified the later fresh same-listener reply (a counter also passes a broken listener), and distinguished an inspected downstream test from the local exercise. The 23ve5 trial log records matching older and later check revisions, an unmatched green result, and absence of recorded rationale. AC-3: the recorded independent agent reader located the evidence. The interaction trial waited for one answer, corrected the deployment inference and accepted stop. AC-4: two focused SkillRegistryTests passed without skips. The rendered review's single offer resolves to the same installed Explain file on three active hosts; alternate vocabulary yields batch and task doc. The recorded trial exercised acceptance, decline and silence. I checked the open wave record and event ledger hashes before and after the public lookup and a source read: both were unchanged. The coordinator's bounded outcome is accurate for 23ve5 Product Intent and 23ve6 Objective in agent exercises. Human understanding and subsequent independent maintenance are unobserved; the broader human outcome is partial.
proposition: qa-reviewer approves the current affected scope
public_path: Rendered Review wave closing offer and the wf-explain pointer on .codex, .claude and .agents -> docs/prompts/explain.prompt.md -> wf_get_change.

command_or_fixture: wf render-surfaces --repo-root <disposable>; full-upgrade main integration test; prompt-name fixture with Batch/Task terms, review-batch slug and three active hosts; wf_get_change on 23tcw and 23tcu.
counterexample_or_failure_condition: the approval predates an affected repair or is not independently grounded
expected: the approving actor independently verifies the current affected scope
known_bad_detection_method: Rendered three independently modified shipped templates through wf render-surfaces in disposable downstream roots. The checks rejected a duplicated review question, removal of the stop-and-wait instruction and permission to credit older runs with newer assertions. All three failed the intended assertion; the unchanged template passed the same checks.
limitations: The existing-project prose merge is agent-guided. Independent render and upgrade checks cover distribution and instructions. Live human teaching outcomes and customized downstream installations remain unobserved.
observed: Public render created the shared prompt and all three host pointers. Public review asked the exact question once and waited; internal review and its skill delegated without repeating it. A second render preserved CRLF custom prose. Renamed review-batch linked to Explain and all host skills used batch/task doc. Upgrade integration passed. Read-only lookup returned the two closed-wave changes and directly resolved the named spec. Seed 160 directs the agent to reconcile an existing custom handoff. The prompt requires version-matched evidence, a single optional teach-back question and no approval or closure changes. Manifest revision matches VERSION.
proposition: A maintainer can enter the same read-only Explain prompt from review or a host skill, find evidence for a closed wave or spec, and see where a recorded test result ceases to support a claim.
safety_and_authorization: Local review evidence only; no external side effects.

observed: Fresh renderer tests passed for all three hosts and Codex alone, including a single offer, identical prompt paths, missing-only CRLF preservation, and an empty second render. Renamed Batch/Task registry, fixed-name parity, real pack membership and public upgrade-main surface phase passed. A separate public render with a valid downstream wf-explain declaration emitted a skill_collision, preserved the downstream skill byte for byte and installed the Explain baseline. Slug, shortcut and alias collisions were each rejected.
proposition: Under the admitted AC-4 and the declared-skill collision contract a fresh render exposes the same Explain prompt via review and every active host; rerender preserves local prompt bytes and a conflicting declared skill survives with a visible diagnostic.
